title: Sibling sweep: propagate filter unknown-key rejection from metadata-server to mail-server (canonical) and remaining 6 *-server siblings
description:
**Pattern source**: bd:JMAP-826m.1 fixed a P0 query-correctness bug in jmap-metadata-server's validate_metadata_filter: a snake_case typo like {"filter": {"related_ids": [...]}} would silently deserialize to MetadataFilterCondition::default() and return ALL objects. The fix added a raw-JSON pre-walk (walk_filter_for_unknown_keys + KNOWN_CONDITION_KEYS allowlist) that rejects unknown keys at every filter-tree node with unsupportedFilter per RFC 8620 §5.5.

**Workspace divergence**: This is a workspace canonical-template violation in the OTHER direction — metadata-server is now stricter than mail-server. The canonical mail-server has:
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:224-238: FLAT unknown-key check on Mailbox/query (works because Option<MailboxFilterCondition>, no operator support).
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs (line ~681): NO unknown-key check on Email/query (Filter<EmailFilterCondition> with operator support — same vulnerability as metadata had).

Per crate-jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, the canonical must change first then propagate. The metadata-server fix landed first because the bead was metadata-scoped; this follow-up sweeps the rest.

**Vulnerable types** (all use Filter<T> with all-Option T fields and no deny_unknown_fields):
- EmailFilterCondition (jmap-mail-types, used by Email/query)
- jmap-mail-types::EmailSubmissionFilterCondition (Email/submissions queries)
- Chat / Message / Space / Contact / Emoji filter types (jmap-chat-types, 5 of them)
- CalendarEventFilterCondition (jmap-calendars-types) + EventNotification
- TaskFilterCondition (jmap-tasks-types) + TaskNotification
- ContactCardFilterCondition (jmap-contacts-types)
- FileNodeFilterCondition (jmap-filenode-types)
- PrincipalFilterCondition + NotificationFilterCondition (jmap-sharing-types)

**Fix shape** (cookie-cut from JMAP-826m.1):
1. Define KNOWN_CONDITION_KEYS const in each server crate matching the per-type wire fields.
2. Add walk_filter_for_unknown_keys recursive walker before typed deserialize in each /query and /queryChanges handler.
3. Add unsupported_filter_unknown_key helper returning a JmapError with description carrying the offending key name.
4. Test pattern per server crate: snake_case typo, unknown leaf field, unknown operator-node field, deeply-nested unknown key, all-known-fields-pass negative control, /queryChanges sibling test.

**Cross-references**:
- Workspace AGENTS.md "Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED" — silent-drop of unknown clauses is a query-correctness bug.
- crate-jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:32-33 — explicit comment forbidding #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on FilterCondition because it breaks #[serde(untagged)] Filter<T>.
- bd:JMAP-826m.1 — the metadata-server fix that established this pattern.

**Suggested decomposition**: child beads per server crate (.1 mail-server canonical, .2 chat-server, .3 calendars-server, .4 tasks-server, .5 contacts-server, .6 filenode-server, .7 sharing-server). Land .1 first; the rest can land in parallel after .1's pattern is canonical.

**Out of scope**: changing the FilterCondition types themselves (they MUST NOT get deny_unknown_fields). The fix is in the server-side handler shim, not in the types crates.
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: where should unknown-filter-key rejection (RFC 8620 §5.5 unsupportedFilter) live? The bead's plan (copy the metadata-server walker into each *-server handler) can't be done as written. The walker no longer exists, and 4 of the 7 siblings (tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing) have no filter-parsing handler of their own because they use the generic jmap-server::handle_query / handle_query_changes.

Options:
A) Add a defaulted associated const to the public QueryObject trait in jmap-types, e.g. `const FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS: Option<&'static [&'static str]> = None;`. Each types crate sets it from a new `pub const <Type>_FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS`, with a drift test like MAILBOX's (bd:JMAP-j7pa.3). One recursive raw-JSON walker in jmap-server would serve both generic handlers: operator nodes may contain only operator and conditions, and condition nodes only keys from the list. The mail-server and calendars bespoke sites (email.rs:785/1034, submission.rs:199, sieve.rs:1063, event.rs:1045) would call that walker before deserializing. This is additive and non-breaking for implementors because of the default, but it extends a public trait.
B) No trait change. Add a `pub fn reject_unknown_filter_keys(filter: &Value, keys: &[&str]) -> Result<(), JmapError>` to jmap-server. Mail and calendars call it directly. Tasks, contacts, filenode and sharing replace their generic handle_query registrations with thin per-type wrappers that call it first. This touches no trait but adds boilerplate and drifts from the generic-handler design.
C) Settle it by policy instead: backends are canonical for filter validation, as for permissions. The server shims stay as they are, and each memory backend rejects unknown keys. This is the least server code, but every third-party backend inherits the silent match-all hazard.

Recommendation: A. It is one walker and one const per filter type, it covers all sites including queryChanges, and the default None means no implementor breaks.

Tests per filter type should use RFC 8620 §5.5 as the independent oracle ("unsupportedFilter: The filter is syntactically valid, but the server cannot process it"; the condition property lists come from RFC 8621 §4.4.1 for Email, RFC 8984/JSCalendar drafts, and so on). Cases: a snake_case typo, an unknown leaf key, an unknown key on an operator node, a deeply nested unknown key, an all-known-keys negative control, and a /queryChanges sibling case.

Exclude chat-server, because its filters are Value passed to the backend. Close or redescribe the bead's metadata-server reference, since that code is gone.

Size: about 250-400 lines across about 10 crates, so roughly L.
DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-19: option A. Defaulted associated const on QueryObject (jmap-types): const FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS: Option<&'static [&'static str]> = None; each types crate sets it from a pub const <Type>_FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS with a drift test (like MAILBOX, JMAP-j7pa.3). One recursive raw-JSON walker in jmap-server used by handle_query/handle_query_changes and the bespoke mail/calendars sites before deserializing -> unsupportedFilter. Non-breaking. Note: chat filters became typed in JMAP-ops7.7 (8baada11), so chat can now participate too. Oracle: RFC 8620 §5.5 + per-type condition lists (RFC 8621 §4.4.1 etc.); cases: typo, unknown leaf, unknown key on operator node, nested, all-known control, /queryChanges.
REVISED by Mark 2026-10-19 (supersedes the walker decision above): use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on every typed *FilterCondition struct AND on jmap_types::query::FilterOperator. Generic handle_query/handle_query_changes already map O::Filter parse failure to unsupportedFilter (jmap-server handlers.rs:315/405); bespoke mail/calendars/chat sites must do the same. Proven compatible with #[serde(untagged)] Filter<T> by a scratch test (serde 1.0.229): leaf, empty leaf, AND/OR, nested NOT parse; unknown leaf key, nested unknown leaf, unknown key on operator node, bad operator all rejected. Correct the false 'deny_unknown_fields breaks untagged' comments (mail-types query.rs:38, chat-types query.rs:18 and siblings); delete chat-types *_FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS if only used for walker rejection. Side effect to test: servers whose O::Filter is a bare condition now reject operator trees with unsupportedFilter instead of silently matching everything. Value-typed filters (calendars-types backend.rs:277, tasks-types backend.rs:211) remain unchecked; note in docs. Tests: RFC 8620 §5.5 quote; typo, unknown leaf, unknown operator-node key, nested, all-known control, /queryChanges, operator tree on a condition-only server.
close_reason: Landed as dc1c19d6 (deny_unknown_fields on filter conditions and FilterOperator; false comments corrected). Review passed. CI green at 8e240e18 (stable+beta 3502 passed).
